# Dual midpoint rigidity: zero nomination

Nielsen–Okamura Conjecture 9.1 remains unresolved in its full smooth, arbitrary-dimensional scope. Root read the derivation and checker. The fourth-order necessary equation has a nonzero derivative kernel at a rank-one cubic, so pointwise injectivity is false. This is not an integrable nonconstant field satisfying the exact midpoint identity. Degenerate-stratum rigidity and higher-order/smooth remainder arguments remain missing.

The known scalar and fixed-tensor-multiple cases, and the companion flat/holomorphic mean classifications, do not cover arbitrary Euclidean dual connections. The fractional Korn extension is excluded by the actual public Mengesha–Scott theorem and the complete projection/rigid-motion bridge in the report.

The root receipt checks private symbolic replay, immutable primary copies, full manifest and historical snapshot copies, reporting live snapshot drift separately. These bounded algebra controls prove no global source result. No Lean, manuscript or credit. Counts stay 9 additional / 39 total, next 40.

# Almost-perfect additive complements: zero nomination

Conjecture 1.3 remains unresolved for all infinite almost-perfect pairs. Root read the report and checker. The full classical factorization bridge supplies the 3/2 lower bound and the gap for genuinely perfect radix pairs. A factorization along bounded-excess subsequences does not give a global radix representation or an upper bound at every intervening scale. The missing stability/transfer from global limsup below 8/5 to limsup at most 3/2 is explicit.

Exact rational support and radix controls establish arithmetic only. Finch Conjecture 14 is also unresolved; its separate small-index capture defect is an uncredited parameter correction. No PROOF.md, Lean, manuscript, acceptance or credit.

The root receipt verifies private exact replay, primary originals/copies, reference snapshot copies, inherited aliases, guard binding and final manifest. Mutable history drift is reported separately. Counts remain 9 additional / 39 total, next 40.

# r201 — Euclidean dual midpoint rigidity remains unresolved

Disposition: one genuinely fresh-to-the-qualified-campaign precise geometric target sustained; zero full ordinary candidates. Root alone adjudicates. Counts stay 9 additional / 39 total, next 40. No PROOF.md, Lean or manuscript.

## Source and literal scope

Frank Nielsen and Kazuki Okamura, *Dual-connection midpoint matrix means and their Gauss composition*, https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.07551, current PDF https://arxiv.org/pdf/2609.07551. The downloaded PDF identifies v2, 22 September 2026, with an internal date September 23. The abstract history gives v1 September 7 14:34:51 UTC and v2 September 22 00:55:11 UTC. No journal DOI or separately verified journal version is established here. Copies were frozen, hashed and verified BEFORE mathematical body reading. Exact retrieval UTC, URLs, bytes and hashes are in http.jsonl and primary-freeze.json.

Conjecture 9.1, printed p39: for EVERY dimension d, connected open Ω⊂R^d, and smooth totally symmetric real cubic tensor field C, define K by <K(X,Y),Z>=C(X,Y,Z) and the Euclidean dual torsion-free connections ∇±=D±K. Let A and M be their local geodesic midpoint branches on a neighborhood of the diagonal. If A(P,Q)+M(P,Q)=P+Q throughout some open neighborhood of the entire diagonal, then C is constant on Ω. The neighborhood may vary with the base point; no global geodesic completeness or uniform neighborhood radius is assumed. The conclusion is constancy in the fixed Euclidean coordinates. Analyticity is NOT assumed.

Read actual Sections 2, 7, 8.6–8.7 and 9, including proofs of Theorems 9.2–9.3. Section 7 proves the converse for every constant symmetric cubic, including nonflat connections in every dimension ≥2. Section 9 establishes the conjecture for d=1 and for C=f C₁ with fixed constant C₁. Those results are already known and are not nominations.

## Uniform route investigated, and its exact gap

Theorem 9.2 gives for all x,h

E_K(x;h)=2K(h,(D_hK)(h,h))+5(D_{K(h,h)}K)(h,h)−4(D_hK)(h,K(h,h))=0.

At a fixed cubic K this is a linear map L_K on the derivative tensor T∈R^d*⊗Sym³(R^d*), obtained by replacing D K with T. If L_K is injective, all first derivatives vanish at that point. A potential all-order route is a dimension-independent kernel/stratum theorem for L_K, followed by a proof that a smooth field satisfying E_K=0 cannot move within its exceptional strata. That would use the source's necessary condition and cover the full midpoint hypothesis without checking arbitrarily many Taylor coefficients.

Exact checks.py constructs every coefficient of E in h and uses rational-domain elimination. In d=2 the cubic coordinates are (C000,C001,C011,C111), derivative coordinates ordered first by differentiation direction and then by that list. At K=(1,0,0,0), L_K has rank 7 of 8 and kernel generated by the single derivative ∂₂C222. At (1,0,0,1), (1,2,3,5), and (0,1,1,0) it has rank 8. Two specified d=3 tensors have rank 30 of 30. These are exact finite algebra, not a uniform injectivity or PDE theorem.

The rank-one obstruction has a simple full algebraic explanation. Set K(v,w)=v₁w₁e₁ and T_v(w,z)=v₂w₂z₂e₂. Then K(h,T_h(h,h))=0, T_{K(h,h)}(h,h)=0 and T_h(h,K(h,h))=0 for every h. Thus L_K(T)=0 despite T≠0. Consequently the unrestricted pointwise injectivity lemma is FALSE, even for nonzero K. This is not a counterexample to Conjecture 9.1: no smooth field on a neighborhood with these prescribed jets and exact midpoint identity is constructed. For example the tempting field C=dx₁³+x₂dx₂³ has this jet at x₂=0 but fails E=0 away from that line; the second scalar block contributes 3x₂h₂⁴. A jet kernel does not establish integrability of a nonlinear PDE solution.

Residual quantifiers: all dimensions d≥2; all smooth tensor fields, including fields whose values lie entirely in degenerate algebraic strata; all base points, even zeros of K; all sufficiently close pairs in a genuine open neighborhood; exact midpoint identity, not finitely many jets. No proof that E=0 forces constancy is available. No proof that the higher even-order conditions overcome the kernel is available. Smooth flat remainders also prevent replacing exact local identity by a formal Taylor series without a separate argument. The finite diagnostic was stopped here; no search expansion substitutes for this missing uniform bridge.

## Closest applicable primary comparison

Kazuki Okamura, *The two-dimensional Matkowski–Sutô equation with holomorphic and strictly increasing generators*, https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.11102, https://arxiv.org/pdf/2609.11102, v1 September 10, 2026 (internal September 11). Frozen before body reading. Read introductory comparison, Definitions 1.1/1.4/1.5, Theorems 1.2/1.6, Lemma 2.2 and Proposition 2.3 with proofs. The holomorphic theorem classifies flat quasi-arithmetic midpoint generators. The shear examples solve midpoint invariance with nonconstant Christoffels but lack Euclidean metric duality. The target source's Remark 9.4 explicitly analyzes this failure: the shear tensor (0,D²F(X′,Y′)) is not totally symmetric unless D²F=0. Hence these are neither source refutations nor a full classical bridge. The target's Section 7 has nonflat examples, so the general problem cannot be reduced to affine generators without proving flatness, which the hypotheses do not imply.

Theorem 8.6 applies scalar classifications only to common autoparallel curves, with the stated geodesic uniqueness conditions. Arbitrary Euclidean lines are not such curves: K(h,h) need not lie in span(h). Thus scalar Matkowski–Sutô classification cannot be asserted to exclude the full conjecture. Original Daróczy–Páles 2002 and Nomizu–Simon 1992 full bodies were not separately retrieved/read; no clearance inferred from their names or summaries. No routine-corollary exclusion is claimed for this target.

## Reconnaissance exclusions, not fresh slots

The Javaheri arrangement and Fradelizi–Manui–Meyer–Ndiaye leads match original r22/r146 records and were stopped as duplicates. The latter PDF was downloaded after the screen in the same sequential tool batch but not read mathematically; it is explicitly unused. No revival of their public-resolved claims or counts.

Fractional Korn's conjecture, Harutyunyan–Mengesha–Mikayelyan–Scott, https://arxiv.org/abs/2302.14588, DOI 10.2140/memocs.2023.11.497, passed the exact original-history alias screen. Read the actual v2 (October 9, 2023) Theorem 1.3, definitions and p4 unnumbered conjecture: extend both quotient and second inequalities to arbitrary bounded Lipschitz domains, every n≥2, 0<s<1, 1<p<∞, without boundary conditions. Current search then found Mengesha–Scott, https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.33325, https://arxiv.org/pdf/2610.33325, v1 submitted October 23, 2026 21:56:25 UTC, internal date October 27. Read Theorems 1.1/1.3 and the latter's proof.

Complete applicable bridge for exclusion: the 2026 Theorem 1.1 asserts (1−s)^−1||u−Πu||_p^p+[u−Πu]_{W^{s,p}}^p≤C[u]_{X^{s,p}}^p for a bounded projection Π onto rigid motions on every bounded Lipschitz Ω and all original n,s,p. Drop the nonnegative first term and use Πu as competitor in the infimum to obtain the original (1.3). For (1.4), the triangle power inequality bounds [u]_W^p by 2^{p−1}([u−Πu]_W^p+[Πu]_W^p). For a rigid motion Ax+b, |A(x−y)|≤|A||x−y|, so its seminorm is ≤|A|^p ∫Ω∫Ω |x−y|^{p−n−sp} dxdy, finite since p(1−s)>0 and Ω bounded. Projection boundedness controls |A| by C||u||_p. Thus the full original second inequality follows with its allowed s-dependent constant. Equivalently the new Theorem 1.3 states it directly for the larger X space, with (1−s)^−1 factor absorbed at fixed s. Definitions of W, X and rigid motions agree literally. This excludes the ENTIRE conjectured Lipschitz extension, not just a boundary-conditioned or p=2 version. It predates this work. No new count.

Also froze/read the introductory scope and Theorems 2.1/2.3 context of Harutyunyan, https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.39437, https://arxiv.org/pdf/2610.39437, October 29, 2026. It cites the still earlier uniform-domain result arXiv:2601.08096 and discusses independent overlapping developments. That cited full body was not read; it is not needed for the direct 2610.33325 bridge. Publication priority among those authors is not adjudicated.

Administrative ledger/NEXT/prior context are snapshots only. Mutable research reports are point-in-time evidence, not immutable scientific originals. Live changes and retained predecessor snapshots are explicitly recorded at finalization.

Live arXiv author search exposed the close companion; the narrow combined keyword search returned no results, illustrating why negative search is not clearance. No current complete public proof-registry head was authenticated: all GitHub API/raw/codeload/diff/patch routes remain denied and unattempted. Cached upstream revision fd4aeeb2ee4fc729c18d98444fed42fd0529eeeb (October 8) is stale and cannot clear current registry history. ScienceDirect and Google challenge routes remain closed; no browser, proxy, retries, bypass, TLS disabling, external messages/uploads or MathDB changes. No new denial occurred. This bounded screen does not establish worldwide unresolved status or priority. All source versions are as retrieved on the actual UTC clock (October 30), despite the environment's local October 29 date.

# Source and exact full-scope target

Weidong Gao and Hanbin Zhang, *On additive bases of finite abelian groups*, https://arxiv.org/html/2610.37136v1. Its current abstract history lists only v1, submitted 27 October 2026 at 12:33:31 UTC. DOI alias 10.48550/arXiv.2610.37136 is an arXiv identifier, not a journal publication claim. Retrieval was on 30 October UTC; execution UTC is authoritative over the environment's initial date. http.jsonl records exact URL, UTC, bytes and SHA256 for every request. Frozen primary copies precede text extraction/body reading. HTML math alttext was retained; experimental HTML and plain extraction limits remain.

Let G=C_p ⊕ C_(pn), p≥5 prime, n≥2 integer, every prime divisor of n at least p. A sequence is finite, unordered, repetitions allowed. It is regular if |S_H|≤|H|−1 for EVERY proper subgroup H<G, including the trivial subgroup. Thus 0 is absent. Σ(S) uses NONEMPTY subsequences; Σ₀ includes the empty sum. The precise surviving Conjecture 1.1 asks c₀(G)=pn+2p−3 for every such pair. Equivalently the upper-bound task is that EVERY regular sequence S with |S|≥pn+2p−3 has Σ(S)=G, together with the known lower bound. It suffices to prove the length-equality upper bound, since subsequences preserve regularity. No bound on support, exponent, n, p, or multiplicities other than regularity is imposed.

Known p-groups and n prime are reconnaissance/public cases, not slots or credits. The primary proves the entire p=3 family and groups outside this boundary family. Its general-prime residual includes n with mixed prime factors, for example p=5,n=35. Any n neither prime nor a p-power with no divisor below p has n≥p², hence n≥2p−1; the Section 7 range covers that residual. A proof only for fixed p=5, large n, cyclic-support sequences or progression sumsets would NOT meet this lane's full target.

Actual source coverage: primary introduction, definitions, Lemmas 2.4–2.12 and their displayed proofs where supplied, all Section 7 Lemmas 7.1–7.3 and proofs, all Section 8 including Lemmas 8.1–8.5 and complete Theorem 1.7 proof. Section 3's Hall formulation was read. The source's citations of old bounds are not treated as read old proof bodies. Middle Sections 4–6 are not fully audited.

# Complete closest public bridge and its limit

Wenkai Yang, https://arxiv.org/html/2610.13103v1, *Additive bases and the zero-sum invariant N(G) for groups C_p ⊕ C_(np)*, submitted 9 October 2026 at 06:57:28 UTC, only v1 listed on the retrieved current abstract. Actual definitions, Kneser formulation, Lemmas 3.1–3.4 with entire proofs, Theorem 3.5 and its proof, and following theorem comparisons were read.

The complete applicable public argument is: with K=pG≅C_n and quotient C_p², the greedy quotient-line procedure of Lemma 3.3 finds k=n−|S_K| disjoint blocks T_i of length≤p, with nonzero sums in K, leaving R whose subset sums hit all K-cosets, provided |S|≥pn+2p²−p−1. The proof first gets a nonzero K-sum from 2p−1 terms in one line: two distinct subset sums have the same quotient image, and another p−1 terms cancel their image; factoring quotient-zero blocks gives one of length≤p with nonzero actual sum. The greedy length reserve ensures this at every step. If the leftover quotient sum is proper, it concentrates all but p−2 terms in one line. Backward maximal-line choice then forces every extracted block into that same line, contradicting regularity in its inverse image.

Replace blocks by their sums, giving n terms in K. If regular over K they cover K by Lemma 3.1 and R fills the quotient. Otherwise choose minimal H₁<K with an overfull compressed sequence. After r=|H₁|−|S_(H₁)|−1 replacements, its H₁ part covers H₁. The stabilizer H₂ of the partial compressed sumset contains H₁; Kneser gives coverage if |S|≥|G|/p+p|K|/p−p+p−2=n(p+1)−2. The final inequality is (|H₂|−p)(|G|/p−|H₂|)≥0, since p≤|H₂|≤|G|/p. Re-expanding disjoint blocks gives actual source subset sums, and the n compressed K terms ensure a nonempty zero sum as well. This supplies every bridge step, with both required length hypotheses, rather than invoking familiar ingredients alone.

Therefore U=max{pn+2p²−p−1,n(p+1)−2}. U−(pn+2p−3)≥2p²−3p+2>0. At p=5,n=35 it is 219 versus 182. This is a rigorous failure of this bound to imply the endpoint, not a refutation or a proof that no better classical adaptation exists. The primary's p=3 proof uses a different low-excess inverse argument to improve it.

Published predecessor: Gao–Li–Qu–Wang, *Additive bases of finite abelian groups of rank 2*, Integers 22 (2022), A37, https://math.colgate.edu/~integers/w37/w37.pdf. Actual title page, introduction, Theorem 1, preliminaries and Lemmas 5–6 proof passages read. Received 10 December 2021, accepted 5 March 2022, published 14 March 2022 as printed. Theorem 1 requires first invariant factor n₁≥2p, whereas ours is n₁=p. No direct applicability follows from large order. Rest of its proof unread. The older 2015/2017/2025 bodies remain unread and must be compared before any future eligibility claim.

# Strongest all-order route and the exact gap

Assume a counterexample at L=pn+2p−3 with n≥2p−1. Since D(G)=pn+p−1≤L and |G|/p+p−2≤L, primary Lemma 2.4 gives trivial stabilizer and nonnegative excess e(T)=|Σ₀(T)|−|T|−1 for every subsequence. For each of the p+1 lines M of V=G/pG, Hall allocates a disjoint (p−1)-term block outside H_M. Each leftover term outside K belongs to exactly one H_M; K terms may be assigned freely, giving A_M. Cauchy–Davenport and the coset product bound give
|Σ₀(A_MT_M)|−1≥|A_MT_M|+(p−1)|A_M|+p e(A_M).
Kneser over the disjoint factors implies
|Σ₀(S)|≥|G|−p(p−1)(p−2)+p Σ_M e(A_M).
Thus Σ e(A_M)≤(p−1)(p−2)−1 for EVERY allowed allocation. Assigning Z=S_K to a line with p−1 remaining terms gives (p−1)|Z|+p e(Z)≤(p−1)(p−2)−1, hence |Z|≤p−3. These are the complete primary reductions, not new credited results.

For p=3 the defect budget is one and Z is empty. The primary obtains progression sumsets in its four line preimages, apart from one explicitly controlled two-term exception, then selects residue slices to fill each K-coset. For p≥5 the budget is ≥11. A=[g,g,4g] with g of order 175 has Σ₀(A)={0,g,2g,4g,5g,6g}, e(A)=2; this six-element set is not an arithmetic progression, checked exactly for every start/difference. It is a regular local sequence in C5⊕C175 supported in a line preimage. It respects the coarse excess budget but is not a complete L-term source counterexample. No claim is made it embeds in one. Consequently the coarse budget alone does not license treating every A_M as a progression.

One complete classical continuation IS available conditionally. Let C_N have no prime divisor below p, and let 2≤k≤p+1 nonempty arithmetic progressions have nonsingleton differences generating C_N. If their sizes sum to at least N+k−1, their sum is C_N. Proof: if proper, take sum stabilizer H. For H=0, Kneser contradicts the size hypothesis. Otherwise write h=|H|,t=[C_N:H], so t≥p. Let r≥1 progressions have nonsingleton differences outside H, s=k−r≤p≤t. Any such progression has size smaller than the order of its quotient difference, or its image is a full nontrivial cyclic subgroup coset stabilizing the quotient sum. Thus its size equals its quotient-image size. Other progressions have singleton quotient image and size≤h. Quotient Kneser, with trivial quotient stabilizer, bounds total size of the r images by t+r−2. Hence total original size≤t+r−2+sh, while N+k−1−(t+r−2+sh)=(h−1)(t−s)+1>0, contradiction. This generalizes the primary's four-progression step with all hypotheses explicit; it is a classical adaptation, not a full resolution.

Missing universal step: for EVERY hypothetical regular source counterexample, produce (possibly after controlled exceptional blocks) appropriate progression/structured slices, and for EVERY x∈V choose compatible residues whose nonempty slices in K have total size at least n+k−1 and whose nonsingleton differences generate K. Must handle all prime p≥5, all residual n including p|n and gcd(p,n)=1, every allowed support and all low-excess exceptional configurations. Neither the excess budget nor quotient averaging currently proves that structural/selection assertion. No universal replacement lemma, proof or counterexample was obtained. No PROOF.md is warranted.

# Almost perfect additive complements: full source question remains open here

The sustained source is Wouter van Doorn, Boning Liu and Quanyu Tang, *On almost perfect additive complements*, https://arxiv.org/html/2610.35027v1, Conjecture 1.3. Its abstract history https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.35027 lists only v1, 26 October 2026 08:40:02 UTC. No DOI is asserted. The literal objects are A,B subset of the nonnegative integers, both infinite, with every sufficiently large integer in A+B. Write A(x)=#(A intersect [0,x]) and similarly B. “Almost perfect” means A(x)B(x)-x does not tend to +infinity. The conjecture is the universal assertion

    limsup_{x→∞} A(x)B(x)/x ∈ {3/2} ∪ [8/5,2].

It is NOT merely the already-public 3/2 lower bound, not only unique representation for every n, and not a finite prefix or one radix family. All initial exceptional integers and all real x tending to infinity belong to its scope. Source Theorem 1.1 is already proved; it receives no nomination. All body bytes were saved, copied and SHA256-bound before the first primary body read. Exact URL/UTC/hash receipts are http.jsonl and primary-freeze.json. The latest abstract was checked after v1 body retrieval and lists no later version.

## Actual closest bodies and the full known adaptation

Read the primary introduction, Lemmas 2.1–2.5, Section 3 proof, Section 4 mixed-radix bounds, and Sections 5.1–5.3. Read Gabardo–Lai, *Spectral measures associated with the factorization of the Lebesgue measure on a set via convolution*, https://arxiv.org/pdf/1311.2209, obtained v1 (9 November 2013 20:37:57 UTC), Theorem 2.2, Lemmas 2.3–2.5 and its full iterative factorization proof (PDF pp6–10). Source bibliography identifies J. Fourier Anal. Appl.20(2014)453–475; the published body was not separately authenticated. The theorem is explicitly attributed there essentially to Lewis; no new factorization machinery is claimed.

Also read Zhang, *A sharp bound for additive complements*, https://arxiv.org/html/2610.29963v1, introduction, Lemma 2.1, Lemma 4.2 counting/convolution proof, and Sections 5–6. This is an October 2026 discrete proof of the SAME 3/2 threshold, not Conjecture 1.3's gap. The body reports a 5 August 2026 announcement of the threshold; that announcement was not independently retrieved. Read Ma, https://arxiv.org/html/2205.04128 (render says v1, 9 May 2022), Lemma 2.1 and its mixed-radix count/limsup construction. Published Ma and 2024 Bárány–Fang–Sándor full bodies were not separately read.

Here is the full applicable bridge, rather than an appeal to familiarity or shortness. Set r(n)=# representations and C(N)=# pairs a,b≤N<a+b. Exactly,

    A(N)B(N)-N = 1 + Σ_{n≤N}(r(n)-1) + C(N).

For large n, r(n)≥1. Bounded excess on a subsequence forces the nondecreasing tail sum of nonnegative integers to be bounded, hence r(n)=1 eventually. Taking a further subsequence N_j gives bounded C(N_j) and A(N_j)B(N_j)/N_j→1. The normalized counting measures have subsequential limits μ,ν with μ*ν=uniform[0,1]: exceptional representations and crossings have O(1) total mass before normalization. Compactness and continuity of convolution prove this statement, without assuming the sets are perfect.

Gabardo–Lai classify μ,ν by alternating convolution digit factors of radices M_i≥2, either stopping with one Lebesgue tail or continuing infinitely. Their proof partitions Fourier zeros of the uniform measure, extracts a periodic factor by Lemma 2.5 and iterates. For the first two factors, let u=M_1 sup(supp ν), which lies in [1-1/M_2,1]. Support endpoints and the first two digit copies give normalized-product lower bounds

    max{2/(2-u), 2/(2-M_2+M_2 u)} ≥ (2M_2+2)/(M_2+2) ≥ 3/2.

The first fraction increases with u, the second decreases; equality in their maximum's minimum is at u=M_2/(M_2+1). For genuinely perfect pairs the full established radix classification and Ma's formula give a complete gap adaptation. Let d_k≥2, D_0=0, D_k=(1-D_{k-1})/d_k and s=liminf D_k. The product limsup is 2/(1+s). If G=limsup d_k<infinity, then d_k≤G eventually and 0<D_k≤1/2. The exact identity

implies D_k≥(1+D_{k-2})/(2G), hence s≥1/(2G-1). Along d_k=G infinitely often, min{D_{k-1},(1-D_{k-1})/G}≤1/(G+1); thus s≤1/(G+1). If G=2, the eventual recurrence contracts to s=1/3 and the limsup is 3/2. If G≥3, 2/(1+s)≥2(G+1)/(G+2)≥8/5. If radices are unbounded, a subsequence has D_k→0 and limsup=2. ## Residual universal obligation

A plausible route would prove the following stability/transfer dichotomy: for every almost-perfect pair whose global limsup is <8/5, bounded-excess subsequential factorization forces its global limsup to be ≤3/2. Together with the known lower bound this proves Conjecture 1.3. This dichotomy is NOT proved here. A single all-binary limiting pair along selected N_j only controls scaled counting functions at those scales and supplies lower bounds; it supplies no upper bound at all intervening or later peak scales. Moving a supremum or limsup through that subsequential convergence would be invalid. Nor do the exact local radix identities construct such a global sequence for arbitrary A,B.
